EASYLOAD   Stephen Lamb.....15

        FASTWORD...again!
        By C.Grant DIXON.
        -----------------
In OUTLET No. 19 Brian Cavers
reviewed a program by Jim Bruce
which was called "Fastword".This
was a thesaurus for the Spectrum
and for anyone who does not know
what a thesaurus is, we can say
that it is a sort of dictionary
in which the words are collected
according to their meaning and
not in alphabetic order. It is
the sort of thing which would be
useful to anyone writing a
literary masterpiece or perhaps
just writing a report for the
boss. Brian has given a good
review and a longer description
in OUTLET 19 so I will refer you
to that for further information.

More recently, Dave Hood of
Betterbytes has combined it with
a much-modified TASWORD 2 to
give a really useful "FASTWORD+"
which he is selling at a very
reasonable price.He's apparently
acquired the rights to the orig-
inal Fastword program when used
with disc systems. Dave has
re-written the TASWORD 2 BASIC.
The disc supplied now contains 5
programs:-
   1. Main load/options menu

   2. FASTWORD+ thesaurus

   3. New TASWORD 2 Basic

   4. TAS 2 Code converter

   5. TAS 2 Text file converter

Note that the TASWORD 2 code
block is NOT supplied for copy-
right reasons and you are
expected to load this from your
own copy. The Code converter is
then used to select suitable
colours and also choose between
the normal font and a new,
specially-designed font which is
much more legible. The code
converter can save TWO blocks of
code and it is suggested that
you have one with dark lettering
on a light ground and the other
with light lettering on a dark
ground.


On entering the main program you
are presented with a menu...

 1. Load Fastword Plus

 2. Load new TASWORD 2

 3. Custom Tasword 2 Code

 4. Instructions

 5. Credits

Let us suppose that you enter
"2" then you have a second
screen asking whether you want
Tascode 1 or Tascode 2. After
this choice you are given the
main Tasword 2 menu page which
can also be called up by typing
STOP (Sym Shift A). This is a
very well-designed page which
offers the following choices...

P  Print file   D  Change drive

S  Save file    E  Erase file

L  Load file    X  Exit

T  Work with text file

G  Define graphic/print codes

B  Save TASWORD 2 Basic + code

F  Load Fastword+

C  Catalogue    H  Help/info

W  Wordcount

Notice the WORDCOUNT facility
which will be very useful to
those who are writing to fill a
given space.

Note also that the new Tasword 2
automatically prefixes all files
with "T.--------" leaving eight
characters for your filename.
When you CATalogue the disc you
will find that only the text
files with this prefix are
shown. For those people who
already have a lot of text files
Dave has supplied a converter
program to add this prefix.


When you opt to load FASTWORD+,
the current text file is saved
to disc to provide room for the
thesaurus. Afterwards the file
is recovered from disc and the
disc file is erased as this was
only for temporary storage.

The FASTWORD+ program is suppli-
ed on disc together with a sheet
of comprehensive instructions
which is an excellent example of
Spectrum Desk Top Publishing in
its own right. I can recommend
this program to anyone who is
already using Tasword 2...it is
a very useful upgrade.

 Price...`9.95

 From:-
       Betterbytes
       10 Spital Terr.
       Gosforth
       NEWCASTLE-upon-TYNE
       NE3 1UT

NETWORK, Review- Malcolm Goodman
--------------------------------
Initially reviewed in 'Computer
Shopper'(Feb.1990), I decided to
take the plunge and ordered five
back issues to see what it was
all about. It took three weeks
and a phone call before my five
tapes arrived in 3(!!)envelopes.

Loading of 4 issues proved to be
impossible due to very weak or
no signal on the tape. The fifth
tape (issue 16) just loaded with
once again a barely useable
signal on the tape. Issue 16 was
duly loaded and it was here my
problems started. Both paper and
ink were set to the same colour
and, with not even a simple
screen message to read, a group
of files were loaded.

Eventually I was presented with
a screen asking me if I wished
to transfer the files to disc
(network is aimed at +D users)so
I opted for the "yes" option.
This transferred the files in
memory to disc, after which the
screen was redrawn to present an
icon-driven menu.

Cursor movement was by keys 6,7,
8,9,0,! (i.e. Non-standard).6&7
were left/right,8/9 for up/down,
and 0 to select. Even at this
point no useful on-screen
instructions had been displayed
as to how to transfer the other
files on the tape to disc.

Two further attempts at getting
the system up and working got me
no further, so, packing up the


four faulty tapes, I wrote to
Barry Turner who publishes this
fanzine, seeking help. Two or
three days later the new tapes
arrived along with a covering
letter from Barry explaining how
to get network onto disc.

Little did I realise that it was
Side B that I should have loaded
first - not Side A! After two
attempts, I finally got NETWORK
up and running.

It was at this point I found the
icon-driven menu was too
sensitive to key presses because
pressing the 0 key for a fract-
ion too long caused the cursor
to remain an arrow instead of
being redrawn as a disc pointer.

Once again I could find nothing
to tell me that only the very
briefest of keypresses was
needed.

However, once I got used to the
system, it was not too difficult
to get it to select the chosen
file(s).

What I did find a bore was the
fact that the icon menu screen
was redrawn each time-and rather
slowly at that.Having done Issue
16,I then decided to transfer an
earlier issue to disc.However,
lack of instruction on how to do
this resulted in my putting
NETWORK aside and since then all
five issues have gathered dust.

Maybe I'm not the quickest at
getting anything up and running
in less than three or four goes
but the almost total lack of
user instructions does not
endear me to NETWORK. I really
do not think that I should have
to write for help to get the
thing working.

Admittedly, Barry was prompt in
replying with a long letter, but
I fail to see why that blank
screen could not be put to
better use.

I like to be supportive of any
user group that treats the
Speccy as other than a pure
games machine but I regret that
until such time as I can get

instructions on how to get any
issue of NETWORK up and running
without a lot of hassle I shall
not be buying any more issues
even at a modest `1 per copy.

For those of you who wish to try
NETWORK, the address is:-

             NETWORK
         38 Kings Drive
            Gravesend
              Kent
            DA12 5BJ

    CASSETTE STORAGE AND THE
    SPECTRUM by Stephen Lamb
    ------------------------
Cassette storage is always slow
and sometimes unreliable but all
Spectrum users have to use it
from time to time no matter what
other storage systems they may
have. The Spectrum is a parti-
cular nuisance when it comes to
using cassette tapes because of
the need to disconnect the ear
plug when saving. I'm sure that
we have all forgotten to do that
at sometime or other. In this
article I will look at a device
which helps to make using
cassette tapes with the Spectrum
easier. I will also give some
advice about maintaining your
cassette recorder.

The Spectrum "Easyload" is a
device which overcomes some of
the problems which occur when
using tape storage with the
Spectrum. It incorporates an
electronic switching system that
obviates the need to disconnect
the ear lead from the tape
recorder when saving. It also
provides two signal outputs when
saving so that you can save two
copies of a program at the same
time providing that you have two
tape recorders.This facility is
particularly useful for Micronet
members since the new Telesoft-
ware Gateway forces you to stay
on line while saving a down-
loaded program.

Since the Easyload enables you
to save two copies of a program
simultaneously, it will reduce
the amount of time you have to
spend on line and therefore your
telephone bills.

The Easyload incorporates some
electronic filtering and
amplification and this should
increase the reliability of the
saving and loading processes.

The Easyload is supplied as a
kit by Maplin Electronics. The
circuit includes five integrated
circuits and two transistors.The
circuit board is not too densely
packed and is quite easy to ass-
emble although I would not reco-
mmend it for absolute beginners
to electronic construction.

I was disappointed that the kit
did not contain any integrated
circuit sockets. I always use
sockets unless there is a good
reason not to. It makes life
much easier if you ever have to
replace the integrated circuits
and reduces the risk of the
components being damaged during
construction.

The instructions supplied with
the kit are comprehensive and
easy to follow. The only problem
which I encountered was that the
front panel drilling details
given in the instructions
appeared to be incorrect. I
found it necessary to modify
them. Check carefully before you
attack the panel with a drill!

My Easyload worked first time.
There is some simple setting up
to be done before the device is
ready for use.This just involves
adjusting two preset resistors
for accurate saving and loading.

The Easyload is connected
between the Spectrum and your
cassette recorder. No modificat-
ions to the Spectrum are necess-
ary since the Easyload is joined
to the Spectrum via the existing
ear and mic sockets. When you
want to save or load, you switch
on the Easyload.There are no
other controls. Operation is
entirely automatic. The Easyload
will indicate via light emitting
diodes whether the signal is
being saved or loaded.

The Easyload is powered by a 9
volt battery. You can use a
rechargeable nicad battery and
provision is made for charging
such a battery via the
Spectrum's own power supply. My
Easyload has been in use for
several months. It has proved to
be reliable and I am very
pleased with it.

I should point out that the
Easyload will not help you if
your saving and loading problems
are due to dirty tape heads or
poor azimuth alignment. Dirty
tape heads can be dealt with
simply with a cleaning cassette.
The azimuth alignment is the
angle at which the tape passes
the heads. It can be adjusted by

turning a small screw which is
usually accessed via a hole near
the playback head. You can only
adjust the screw when the
cassette player is in play mode.
You can alter the the azimuth
alignment by playing a tape and
then adjusting the screw for
maximum output. However, this is
a bit hit and miss. For greater
accuracy, use an azimuth
alignment tape. I use Global
Software's Operation Caretaker.
The alignment tape first loads a
programme into the Spectrum and
then sends a stream of data. The
screen display tells you whether
or not the data is being receiv-
ed correctly. If it isn't, you
turn the screw until it is. The
azimuth alignment is then set.

The Spectrum Easyload kit is
available from...


       Maplin Electronics,
      P.O. Box 3, Rayleigh,
         Essex. SS6 2BR.


The catalogue number is LK39N
and it costs `11.95. The reco-
mmended case has the catalogue
number LL08J and costs `4.45.

I have not seen Operation Care-
taker in the shops for some time
but Interceptor Software produce
an azimuth alignment tape for
the Spectrum which costs about
`5.00.
                - Stephen Lamb.

### FASTWORD... again!
*By C.Grant DIXON.*

In OUTLET No. 19 Brian Cavers reviewed a program by Jim Bruce called "Fastword". This was a thesaurus for the Spectrum—a dictionary where words are collected by meaning rather than alphabetically. It's useful for literary work or business reports. I refer you to OUTLET 19 for Brian's original review.

More recently, Dave Hood of Betterbytes has combined it with a modified TASWORD 2 to create "FASTWORD+", which he sells at a very reasonable price. He acquired the rights to the original Fastword for disc systems and rewrote the TASWORD 2 BASIC. The disc now contains 5 programs: Main menu, FASTWORD+ thesaurus, New TASWORD 2 Basic, TAS 2 Code converter, and TAS 2 Text file converter.

Note: The TASWORD 2 code block is NOT supplied due to copyright. You must load this from your own copy. The Code converter allows choosing colours and a new, more legible font. It can save two code blocks (e.g., dark/light and light/dark).

The main program menu offers: 1. Load Fastword Plus, 2. Load new TASWORD 2, 3. Custom Tasword 2 Code, 4. Instructions, 5. Credits.

Tasword 2 is accessed via the menu or by typing STOP (Sym Shift A). It includes a useful WORDCOUNT facility. Note that the new Tasword 2 prefixes all files with "T.--------". A converter is included for existing files. When FASTWORD+ is loaded, the current text file is saved temporarily to disc and restored afterwards. It's a very useful upgrade for existing Tasword 2 users.

**Price:** £9.95
**Contact:** Betterbytes, 10 Spital Terr., Gosforth, NEWCASTLE-upon-TYNE, NE3 1UT

***

### NETWORK
*Review by Malcolm Goodman*

I ordered five back issues of this fanzine after reading a review. It took three weeks and a phone call to receive them. Four tapes failed to load; the fifth (issue 16) barely loaded. The system appeared to be for +D users, transferring files to disc via an icon-driven menu. The controls (6,7,8,9,0) were non-standard, and the lack of on-screen instructions made it frustrating.

After writing to the publisher, Barry Turner, I received new tapes and a letter explaining how to get it working (load side B first). Even then, the menu was too sensitive to key presses, and the slow screen redraws made it a chore. I gave up on it, and the issues have been gathering dust since. While Barry was helpful in his correspondence, the lack of accessible, built-in documentation makes it hard to recommend, despite the modest price of £1 per copy.

**Address:** NETWORK, 38 Kings Drive, Gravesend, Kent, DA12 5BJ

***

### CASSETTE STORAGE AND THE SPECTRUM
*By Stephen Lamb*

Cassette storage is slow and occasionally unreliable. The Spectrum is particularly annoying because one must disconnect the ear plug when saving. The "Easyload" device helps here by incorporating an electronic switching system, removing the need to unplug the lead. It also provides two signal outputs to save two copies of a program simultaneously—useful for Micronet users reducing online costs.

Easyload improves reliability through filtering and amplification. It is supplied as a kit by Maplin Electronics. It includes five ICs and two transistors; while easy to assemble, it's not for absolute beginners. I was disappointed that no IC sockets were provided. The instructions were mostly good, though the front panel drilling details were incorrect. Easyload is powered by a 9V battery, which can be recharged via the Spectrum’s power supply.

**Price:** £11.95 (Cat No: LK39N), Case: £4.45 (Cat No: LL08J).
**Supplier:** Maplin Electronics, P.O. Box 3, Rayleigh, Essex, SS6 2BR.

### FASTWORD... снова!
*Автор: C.Grant DIXON.*

В OUTLET №19 Брайан Каверс делал обзор программы Джима Брюса под названием "Fastword". Это тезаурус для Spectrum — своего рода словарь, в котором слова сгруппированы по смыслу, а не в алфавитном порядке. Он полезен для написания литературных произведений или деловых отчетов. Подробности можно найти в 19-м выпуске.

Недавно Дэйв Худ из Betterbytes объединил его с модифицированным TASWORD 2, получив очень полезный "FASTWORD+". Дэйв приобрел права на оригинальный Fastword для дисковых систем и переписал BASIC от TASWORD 2. Диск содержит 5 программ: главное меню, тезаурус FASTWORD+, новый BASIC для TASWORD 2, конвертер кода TAS 2 и конвертер текстовых файлов TAS 2.

Примечание: сам блок кода TASWORD 2 НЕ прилагается из-за авторских прав, его нужно загрузить со своей копии. Конвертер кода позволяет настраивать цвета и выбирать новый, более читабельный шрифт. Можно сохранить два блока кода (например, светлый на темном и наоборот).

Меню программы включает: 1. Загрузка Fastword Plus, 2. Загрузка нового TASWORD 2, 3. Настройка кода Tasword 2, 4. Инструкции, 5. Кредиты. В Tasword 2 добавлена полезная функция WORDCOUNT (счетчик слов). Новая версия добавляет к именам файлов префикс "T.--------", для старых файлов есть конвертер. При запуске FASTWORD+ текущий текст временно сохраняется на диск, а затем восстанавливается. Отличное обновление для пользователей Tasword 2.

**Цена:** £9.95
**Адрес:** Betterbytes, 10 Spital Terr., Gosforth, NEWCASTLE-upon-TYNE, NE3 1UT

***

### NETWORK
*Обзор: Malcolm Goodman*

Заказав пять старых номеров этого фэнзина, я ждал их три недели. Четыре кассеты не загрузились, пятая (выпуск 16) — с трудом. Система оказалась рассчитана на пользователей +D и требует переноса файлов на диск через иконное меню. Управление (клавиши 6,7,8,9,0) нестандартное, подсказок на экране нет. 

После письма издателю Барри Тернеру я получил новые кассеты и инструкцию (надо загружать сторону B). Даже зная это, меню оказалось слишком чувствительным к нажатиям, а экран перерисовывался очень медленно. В итоге я забросил это дело. Несмотря на вежливость Барри, отсутствие нормальной документации делает систему неудобной. Не рекомендую, даже при цене £1 за номер.

**Адрес:** NETWORK, 38 Kings Drive, Gravesend, Kent, DA12 5BJ

***

### ХРАНЕНИЕ НА КАССЕТАХ И SPECTRUM
*Автор: Stephen Lamb*

Кассеты — это медленно и ненадежно, но все пользователи Spectrum сталкиваются с ними. Проблема Spectrum в необходимости отключать разъем EAR при сохранении. Устройство "Easyload" решает эту задачу с помощью электронной коммутации. Оно также позволяет записывать сразу две копии программы на два разных магнитофона — полезно для пользователей Micronet для экономии на телефонных счетах.

Easyload улучшает надежность за счет фильтрации и усиления сигнала. Продается в виде набора (kit) от Maplin Electronics. В схеме пять микросхем и два транзистора; собирается легко, но не для новичков. Минус — в наборе нет панелек для микросхем. Инструкции хорошие, но данные для сверления передней панели неверны. Питание — от батарейки 9В с возможностью подзарядки от БП Spectrum.

**Цена:** £11.95 (Кат. № LK39N), корпус: £4.45 (Кат. № LL08J).
**Поставщик:** Maplin Electronics, P.O. Box 3, Rayleigh, Essex, SS6 2BR.
